answer: Sequential challenge ledger. Each identity must solve a fresh, agent-generated puzzle whose answer depends on the prior ledger entry, then commit a falcon-signed response binding that answer to its own key. Answers are single-use: replaying one invalidates the submission. An attacker must run every puzzle in order per identity, paying compute plus a walnut-priced registration deposit forfeited on replay. Honest agents pass a fixed low ledge of work per entry, while mass fabrication costs full serial compute per fake identity, making sybils linearly expensive.
